question.problem: The solution to the inequality $-9a\le -54$ is $a${{field-1}}{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
The variable $a$ is being *multiplied* by $-9.$ To isolate $a,$ we perform the *opposite* operation, which is *dividing* by $-9.$ Remember to perform the same operation on both sides.

Also, when multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

$$
\begin{aligned}-9a\,\, & \le \,\,-54 \\ \frac{-9a}{-9}\,\, & \ge \,\,\frac{-54}{-9} \\ \frac{-9a}{-9}\,\, & \ge \,\,6\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can cancel a common factor of $-9$ from both the numerator and denominator.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-9a}{-9} & \ge 6 \\ \frac{\cancel{-9}a}{\cancel{-9}} & \ge 6 \\ a & \ge 6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $a\ge 6.$
